bandReport.notes: BAND RANGE vs ASSIGNMENT: I was told to expect 'roughly 86-100', but the pages carry 81-100 and I trusted the pages as instructed. Idx 18 opens at item 81 at the top of c1 with clear whitespace above it, so 81-85 are whole on my pages and are transcribed here. If band b4 also reported 81-85 the merge dedupes them; if b4 stopped at 80 they would otherwise have been a silent gap, which is why they are included. PAGE MAPPING: idx 18 = printed 37, idx 19 = printed 39, idx 20 = printed 41, idx 21 = printed 43 - only odd printed pages are present, i.e. the English side of a bilingual booklet. Items per page: 81-85 (idx 18), 86-90 (idx 19), 91-96 (idx 20), 97-100 (idx 21). No item spills past either band edge. ITEM 100 IS PRESENT AND COMPLETE - stem, both numbered statements, the 'Which of the above statements is/are correct?' line and all four options are whole at the foot of p21-c2, and it is the last item in the paper. The footer of that last content page still prints '[ P.T.O.' even though the paper ends there; that is a booklet quirk, not a missing page. COLUMN CROPS: all eight crops split cleanly on the gutter. No line is sliced down its middle, no item number is missing from the top of any c2, and no option block is orphaned from its stem. The only artefact is cosmetic - on each page the centred page number sits close to the split, so the last digit of the printed folio bleeds into the bottom-left of c2 ('7' on idx 18, '9' on idx 19, '1' on idx 20, '3' on idx 21). No question text was lost or duplicated by it and I did not need to fall back to any pNN.png for reading order. Show-through ghosting of the Hindi reverse side is visible on all four scans and never obscures the English text. TRANSCRIPTION CHOICES: (1) This paper numbers its statement lists with ARABIC numerals ('1.', '2.', '3.') and its options refer to them the same way ('1 and 2'), unlike the 2025 paper's Roman numerals - transcribed as printed. (2) Items 87, 90 and 96 print an emphasis word in bold italic ('best', 'best', 'not'); no bold markup is carried, the word is transcribed as plain text in place. (3) Typographic quotes and apostrophes normalised to ASCII; no words changed. (4) The booklet's space-before-colon style ('statements :', 'Statement 1 :', 'Awards :') is preserved as printed. (5) Item 97 prints 'Statement 1 :' / 'Statement 2 :' as headed blocks; those headings are kept on their own lines inside the stem. SOFT SUBTOPICS not in catalog.json, flagged for possible extension: 'Citizenship' (item 89, under Polity and Governance > Constitutional Framework and Philosophy - citizenship is Part II of the Constitution and none of the listed subtopics there covers it) and 'Tribal Languages' (item 95, under History > Art and Culture - the listed subtopics cover architecture, literature, painting, performing arts, festivals and national symbols, none of which is a language question). CLASSIFICATION NOTE: item 84 asks for the nodal ministry of the Forest Rights Act, 2006; filed under Environment and Ecology > Forests and Natural Resource Management > Forest Rights and Community Forestry, which names the subject matter exactly, rather than under Polity and Governance. No question in this band contains mathematics, so there are no LaTeX zones and no tables. No duplicated option text and no defective item found.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements :
1. 'Right to the City' is an agreed human right and the UN-Habitat monitors the commitments made by each country in this regard.
2. 'Right to the City' gives every occupant of the city the right to reclaim public spaces and public participation in the city.
3. 'Right to the City' means that the State cannot deny any public service or facility to the unauthorized colonies in the city.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
